pages.text: An AE2 network needs to be chunkloaded for any of its $(l:ae2_mechanics/devices)devices$(/l) to be able to function, and if only some of it is loaded, it may not function correctly. The Spatial Anchor solves this problem. It forceloads the chunks that its network occupies. A single cable extending across a chunk border is enough to load that new chunk.

It will propagate its "loading" across $(l:items_blocks_machines/quantum_bridge)quantum bridges$(/l), but not cross-dimensionally, so if you have a quantum bridge to the nether, you need a spatial anchor on the network in your base and on the network in the nether.$(br2)By default it will also enable random ticks in its loaded chunks, this can be turned off in the ae2 config.$(br2)It can be rotated with a $(l:items_blocks_machines/wrench)Certus Quartz Wrench$(/l) if for
some reason you want to do that.

pages.title: Settings
pages.text: $(li)The spatial anchor provides access to the global setting to view energy in AE or E/FE.$(li)An in-world hologram can be displayed showing the chunks being loaded.

pages.title: Energy
pages.text: The spatial anchor will use $(l:ae2_mechanics/energy)energy$(/l) according to this equation:$(br2)e = 80 + (x\$(o)(x+1))/2$()$(br2)where x is the number of chunks being loaded
